description:

title: Soft Skills That AI Cannot Replace Yet
60% of new managers fail within 18 months (avoid 3 common mistakes)
description:
60% of new managers fail within 18 months — here are 3 common mistakes to avoid (and what you can do instead):

1/ Stop solving every problem yourself (instead, ask your team questions to get their understanding, context, opinion, recommendation, and then co-solve the puzzle together).

2/ Stop leading with unclear expectations (instead, make your standards explicit and tell your team that auditing is part of your job and is how you stay close to the details, provide your team with a clear "How to work with me" doc that explains SOP, communication preferences, and FAQs to proactively answer). 

3/ Stop relying on short-term motivation speeches (instead, create momentum through repeated wins, big and small, because progress compounds).

A key shift from IC to Manager is you stop being judged just on your output.

Rather, you start being judged on what your team can repeatedly accomplish without you.

description:

In this lightning lesson by Sally Ivester (Google) & Jason Yoong (Level Up & ex-Amazon), you'll learn how to shift from doing more to being seen as a leader, so decision-makers recognize you as ready for the next level.

description:
Renowned author and filmmaker Leon Logothetis (aka The Kindness Guy) and Jason Yoong (COO at Level Up) discuss Leon's journey to find the meaning of life, his new film on Amazon Prime Video "The Kindness Within: A Journey to Freedom", and his thoughts on how hard-working/smart/ambitious professionals can strive for more beyond the fancy title and paycheck (Leon is a former broker).

---------
About Leon Logothetis
Before becoming a global adventurer, TV host, motivational speaker, and bestselling author, Leon Logothetis lived an uninspired life as a broker in London. Though seemingly successful, he was chronically depressed. To change this, he gave it all up for a life on the road fueled by giving and receiving kindness.

​Traveling to over 100 countries, he found humanity's essence and the bonds connecting people worldwide. Through kindness, he saw that comparing similarities rather than differences creates a brighter future.

​For over a decade, Leon has inspired the world with his message of kindness and hope. This shines through in his hit TV show "The Kindness Diaries" on Discovery Plus.

​When not making shows and writing, Leon travels speaking about kindness, compassion, and empathy. His goal is to make a positive impact. He also founded Winston Entertainment, producing content highlighting humanity's good.

​Leon has partnered with top companies including Amazon, Starbucks, Southwest, Delta, Bombas, United Way, 3M, TED, W Hotels, Zendesk, US Air Force, Charles Schwab, SXSW, Spectrum, and more.

Follow Leon on Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/thekindnessguy

---------
About Leon's new film "The Kindness Within: A Journey to Freedom"
​(watch on Amazon Prime Video)

​It takes extraordinary courage to put down a suicide note, pick up the book of a mystical yogi, and travel to an ancient land in a desperate search for life. Together, Leon and the viewers are guided by spiritual leaders, helpers of humanity, and even the universe, or as some people call it, God. Leon walks on the sand by the Ganges and speaks hushed Sufi prayers under the stars. He talks to living saints and serves food for hundreds of thousands in the hot, smoke-filled halls of God’s kitchen. He dances to exhaustion in the marble temples of the Hari Krishna and meditates with Buddhist monks in the Himalayas. Through it all, Leon comes to discover that the true meaning of life is not an external pursuit, but rather an intimate exploration of the kindness, love, and purpose already within us all.

title: Interview FAQs- How to Answer the Hardest Interview Questions
description:
In this excerpt from a live stream, Ethan Evans breaks down how to answer tough interview questions, from handling conflict with a coworker to discussing your biggest weakness and addressing gaps in your resume. This talk is packed with actionable insights to help you navigate job interviews confidently.

Timestamps & Key Takeaways:

• 00:00:00 – Introduction: How to handle difficult interview questions
• 00:00:19 – How to talk about workplace conflict using the STAR method
• 00:02:13 – Why interviewers ask conflict-related questions & what they are looking for
• 00:03:03 – The “Biggest Weakness” trap question—what NOT to say
• 00:04:19 – Real weaknesses vs. fake weaknesses (and how to frame them properly)
• 00:05:09 – Tips on demonstrating self-awareness and personal growth
• 00:05:47 – Which interview questions you should decline to answer (illegal or inappropriate questions)
• 00:08:06 – How companies use sneaky tactics to gather personal information
• 00:09:58 – How to discuss past jobs that ended on a bad note (without badmouthing anyone)
• 00:12:30 – Handling the question: “Why were you laid off?”
• 00:14:32 – How to talk about a failure in an interview (What was the failure? What did you learn? What would you do differently?)
• 00:17:24 – What to do if you don’t know the answer to a coding question in an interview
• 00:18:54 – The hiring decision process: How many no votes mean rejection?
• 00:21:17 – The impact of attitude in interviews—why anger and frustration work against you
• 00:23:17 – How to explain gaps in your resume (and turn them into positives)
• 00:26:10 – What interviewers really want to know about you
• 00:26:52 – The right way to answer “Tell me about yourself” (without oversharing)
• 00:30:14 – How much time should you spend preparing stock answers for interview questions?

 Key Takeaways:

✔ Use the STAR method (Situation, Task, Action, Result) for structured responses
✔ Avoid fake weaknesses (e.g., “I work too hard”)—be honest but show self-improvement
✔ Never answer illegal questions (e.g., age, marital status, race, or personal background)
✔ Frame past job exits in a positive light—focus on what you’re moving toward, not what you’re leaving
✔ When discussing failures, highlight what you learned and how you improved
✔ If stuck on a technical question, ask for hints rather than wasting time
✔ Be mindful that attitude and confidence can make or break your chances

title: Lessons from Jeff Bezos & Elon Musk
description:
🔔 Subscribe for more executive insights & career growth strategies!

In this excerpt from a conversation with @cloudwithraj  former Amazon VP Ethan Evans shares what it was really like to work with Jeff Bezos and interview with Elon Musk.

👉 Learn how Jeff evaluates projects, how he handles crisis situations, and why Ethan walked out of an Elon Musk interview.

Timestamps & Key Takeaways

⏳ 00:00 – Introduction: Working with Jeff Bezos & Elon Musk
 
⏳ 00:30 – Jeff Bezos’ 3-Question Framework for Evaluating Projects

📌 Jeff asks three critical questions before approving new ideas:

1️⃣ Is it real? – Can this product be built, or is it just theoretical?
2️⃣ Is it worth it? – Does it have significant market & revenue potential?
3️⃣ Can we win? – Do we have the competitive advantage to dominate?

 Example: Why Amazon consistently rejected proposals to enter banking & financial services.

⏳ 03:34 – What It’s Like to Be in a Meeting with Jeff Bezos

 Jeff’s humor & personality: Despite his tough decision-making, Jeff is funny & self-aware.

Handling crisis with humor: How Jeff joked about a public scandal to ease tension in an Amazon leadership meeting.

How Bezos deals with controversy: The high-stakes internal investigation that uncovered the truth behind leaked private messages.

⏳ 07:27 – Interviewing with Elon Musk for a VP Role at SpaceX

💡 Ethan got a cold call for a VP of Software position at SpaceX, reporting directly to Elon Musk.

🛑 Why Ethan walked out of the interview:
 • Musk expected executives to code (even 10% of their time).
 • Recruiting miscommunication: Ethan had clarified he wasn’t a hands-on coder anymore.
 • Ethan’s realization: “Do I really want to ride a rocket with my part-time code?” 🤔

 What this says about Elon’s leadership style:
 • Extreme expectations for hands-on leadership.
 • Willing to debate & push back, but expects full alignment with his vision.

⏳ 11:58 – Final Thoughts: The Legacy of Ownership & Leadership at Amazon

🎯 Ethan co-crafted Amazon’s “Ownership” leadership principle, shaping how Amazon leaders think about accountability and decision-making.

📢 Key Takeaways from Jeff Bezos & Elon Musk
 • Jeff’s 3-question framework is a powerful tool for evaluating big bets.
 • Leadership at the highest levels requires humor, resilience, and tough decision-making.
 • Elon’s extreme hands-on approach sets him apart, but isn’t for everyone.
 • Know your non-negotiables—Ethan walked away because the expectations didn’t align.

0:25 Step 1: Do Your Job Well – Ensure your manager isn’t dissatisfied with your performance.
0:54 Step 2: Ask Your Manager How You Can Help – Build a strong relationship with your boss.

title: Inside The Ukraine Conflict: Discussion with Ethan Evans & Lena Mykhailova
description:
Get the real human story of the conflict in Ukraine. Not the politics, but the on-the-ground experience from a woman who has lived it for three years. Lena Mykhailova, our head of Ukrainian Refugee Relief, joined me (Ethan) live from Kyiv to share very real experiences both from her own life and the others we serve. We also took a few audience questions on how people can get involved. 

Note: In the video from 0:01:51-0:05:07 and then from 0:56:37-1:00:05 Lena dropped from Zoom due to electrical blackouts and needing time to switch on the generators. We kept it in the recording because it is the reality of the situation.

I met Lena near the start of the war, in March, 2021. She had escaped Poltava, Ukraine, near the front lines of the conflict and the embattled region of Kharkiv with her family. Lena's husband volunteered for the army even though he is distinctly middle age (40+) and fought for more than two years. Lena herself came with her sons to Krakow, where she became head of refugee services for our Ukrainian Community Center.

Money goes a long way in Poland and we are very efficient. We are able to provide services to an entire displaced family for $25 / month.

Because men between 18 and 60 must stay in the country to fight, most refugees are women, children, elderly, and disabled. Those most vulnerable and in need.

Learn more about the center: https://kochamdebniki.pl/

You can donate to support the work via PayPal or bank transfer here: https://kochamdebniki.pl/donation/

If you want a tax receipt, you can go through our US partner, the Hispanic Counsel of Chautauqua County: https://www.paypal.com/donate/?hosted_button_id=WMYJHS9UVMWY2

title: The art of making the other VP realize his mistakes without saying so
description:
In this conversation, Yuzheng Sun (Staff Data Scientist at Statsig; Prev. Meta, Amazon, Tencent) interviews Ethan Evans (retired Amazon VP) on the essence of effective leadership and management within tech companies. 

Key takeaways:
1/ Ethan underscored that a manager's true power lies not in their individual contributions but in how they harness the collective strengths of their team. He stressed the importance of nurturing all team members—from top performers to those who may be struggling—highlighting that overlooking any segment could be a costly mistake.

2/ Ethan illustrated the multifaceted role of managers as negotiators and influencers. They had to adeptly manage peer relationships, dependencies, and resources to create an environment for innovation. As leaders ascended to director-level positions, their focus shifted to making strategic impacts on the company — driving revenue, reducing costs, and enhancing customer satisfaction.

3/ A particularly compelling part of the discussion revolved around influencing others without authority. Ethan shared his experience at Twitch, where, without formal power, he effectively guided leadership by asking, "Could I share how I've seen this done elsewhere?" This approach opened doors to collaboration, allowing leaders to present valuable insights without triggering defensiveness.

4/ Ultimately, Ethan emphasized the importance of building trust and demonstrating genuine intent to help. By positioning oneself as a collaborative partner rather than an adversary, leaders could influence decisions and drive positive change, even in challenging situations.

title: Managing Up with Ethan Evans & Ella Irwin
description:
I was happy to be a guest on the CryRoom Podcast where I joined Ella Irwin to discuss Managing Up, an important skill that people need to master for career success. Regardless of where you are in your career, you may suddenly be reporting to someone new, who has a different style than you are used to and you will need to quickly figure out how best to work with this person. You need to create a great partnership with your manager and this episode will give you actionable guidance on how to do this. This episode covers all of the following:

1. What is managing up and why is it important?
2. Ways to determine your manager’s style.
3. What questions to ask your manager to better understand their needs.
4. Managing up vs setting boundaries.
5. How to manage up when you make a big mistake and impact your manager/ team/ company and rebuild trust.
6. What happens if your manager leaves? Was it all for nothing?

One team member had 2 years, one had 1 year, and 3 were new college grads. Thus, Ameesh had more experience than the other 5 members combined.

​Ameesh is a natural leader and took the role of lead engineer on the first version of Prime Video.

​While working with me, Ameesh was promoted first to SDE III, then switched to Manager. He was promoted to Senior Manager (Amazon L7) while working on Prime Video.

​Ameesh and I switched to video games and then to build the Amazon Appstore. Ameesh moved to Orange County to be closer to his family. He built a new office for the Amazon Appstore, ultimately with 300 people, and was promoted to Director (Amazon L8).

​Ameesh left Amazon to found his own startup, Atom Tickets.

title: Real Resume Review | Account Management
description:

title: How Executive Search Works | The Benefits of Diversity
description:
Numerous studies have shown that diversity in the workplace increases performance for the team and the business. When co-workers are from different backgrounds they bring different thoughts and ideas. This leads to an increase in innovation that in turn will produce a higher quality product or service. It’s simple: employees just perform better when there are different viewpoints and opinions.

Watch Ethan Evans, former VP of Twitch Prime at Amazon, talk about how executive search works and the challenges that it entails.

Ethan Evans’ views are his own and he is not speaking on behalf of Amazon or Twitch.

Specific Questions Discussed:

How does executive job search work?
Will recruiters / hiring managers consider executives from different industries?
Is there a better way to apply for a job than the company’s website?
If I am under qualified, how can I still get an interview?
How do you prepare for an executive interview?
What’s the best way for a new manager to climb the career ladder?

title: How to Pace Your Career for Long Term Success and Fulfillment
description:
Every life has seasons. There will be periods when you have lots of time and energy for your job and times when you struggle to hang on. How should you manage these variations? 

You can have a very successful career without always working flat out. Some types of work build this in, with natural crunch periods. Accountants have the quarterly and year-end closings, as well as tax season. Many retailers have a fourth-quarter push. Video game development is famous for crunch time. All college students recognize midterms and finals week as a type of crunch, and “spring break” as a literal break.

On a more personal level, how can you anticipate some of these periods to best manage them? What can you do when you suddenly find yourself burnt out or forced to take an unexpected pause? What about when things are going your way? How can managers pace their team's crunch time? How can "A career is a marathon and not a sprint" be interpreted in your own professional trajectory?

title: The Secret to Grow your Career Without Managing People
description:
Many people associate career growth with the need to go into management, but this not so. There is no doubt that one path to career progression, both in terms of money and impact, can be to lead others. But, you can lead others without managing them. Most larger corporations, as an example, have what is called a dual-track. They have parallel titles, levels, and compensation for individuals who are experts in a skill but who do not manage others.

To rise up such a track you must develop your core skill in your profession to be finely tuned and to be worth additional money. You must raise your value to the company so where they feel your impact merits a bigger title and more compensation.

No matter how skilled you are at your craft, whether finance, art, law, or another specific skill, there will come a time where you probably need to lead in some degree even though you do not manage. Management means specifically directing other people, including the “human resources” aspects, such as compensation, reviews, and complaints or problems. To grow, you do not need to take on these duties. But you will need to develop the ability to explain your expert work to others and to help them make the overall project or product more valuable based on your input. You may want to work on your craft in isolation, but this is rarely possible in a corporation.

title: Which Risk Should You Take? Veteran Leader Shares His Secret Strategy
description:
When does a decision become a risk or a gamble? 

Everyone loves to gamble when they feel sure they will win.  After all, a bet you are going to win is not really a bet at all.  At work, we get ahead by making smart decisions.  But when decisions become unclear, they start to feel risky.  Different people, and different companies, handle these unclear decisions in very distinct ways.

At some level, all decisions have risk.  If one alternative was so clearly better than the other, with no downside whatsoever, you probably wouldn’t even consider the alternative.  When a decision has ambiguity as to the outcome or trade-offs that are not fully predictable, we start to call it a risk.  If we feel it is particularly risky, out of our control, or uncertain, we call it a gamble.  The terms are not precise, but very broadly if we believe something is 90% or more likely to work out as we plan we tend to term it a decision or a choice.  Around 70/30 we call it a risk, and when it starts to feel like a 50/50 coin flip, we call it a gamble.

To take smart risks we have to do three distinct things:

1) Recognize that there is a decision being made with alternatives and consequences that are not fully predictable or controllable

2) Identify what things are controllable and work to control them.  Amazon calls these the controllable inputs.

3) Consider the consequences of the decision not working out, of the risk being realized, and what you can do if that happens

Some decisions will not work out how we planned.  We can skew the odds in our favour by recognizing them and controlling what we can. We can improve the results by considering our response to a bad outcome upfront.

In the end, smart risks are those where you can skew the odds in your favour and where you can accept the consequences if it does not work out.  Dumb risks are those where either you don’t even recognize the possibility of a bad outcome or you fail to take steps to prepare for it.

title: How to Lead | Effectively Solve Ego problems at Work
description:
Ego is more than just arrogance. Yes, one workplace problem comes from people who cannot hear other opinions or admit mistakes due to classic ego. This EZ Coach discussion will go beyond simple egotism, to the broader challenges that arise any time someone’s self-worth or self-identity, their ego, is threatened.

All human beings have a pain and distress threshold. When you exceed this tolerance, the person will act to relieve the distress. The more painful the circumstance, the less discretion the person will show in trying to eliminate the perceived problem. And often you either are that problem or you get caught up in reaction.

Often when someone says no to us, criticizes our work, or even attacks us personally, the underlying cause can be their own internal distress. One way or another, something is threatening their ego, defined as their self worth or image. The person is lashing out to reduce their own pain and catching us as they do it. Saying yes to us may make more work for them than saying no. Our work may threaten their own projects, priorities, or personality. In the worst case, they may depart from even a semblance of the business rationale and simply attack to drive us away or vent their own rage.

What can we do in such circumstances? Come join the EZ Coach and let’s talk about it! 

NOTES:-
1. What is ego?
• "Ego is the part of us that is judged by others"
• The ego develops to protect you
• Selective Reasoning
• To rationalize something bad
• "I've got a story for this"
• Helps us feel good

2. Ego at work
• When someone is judged
• It's hard to tell your boss you screwed up
• Moves from "responding to the problem" to "resisting work"
• Hard to say "I can't do everything", so they push to someone else
• Medicating the pain unknowingly

3. Understanding your own ego
• Not all negative feedback is other's ego
• The lesson one in dealing with ego is to "understand your own ego"

4. How to deal with ego?
• Recognize and understand his pain
• Look for- 
"Are they overworked?"
"Is your request difficult for them?"
• Empathize
• Don't let your ego involved as well
• "Would it be better if we discuss this another time?"
• Take witness

5. Busy vs ego
• Busy people- do they get a lot done?
• Assume good intent
• "Don't contribute to malice"
• Most people just want an easy great life
• People usually want to do a good job
• Are they having something else going in their lives?

6. SBI rule
• Don't jump straight to criticism- have a relation first
• Ego gets threatened more in public
• Praise in public, criticize in private
• Situation-Behaviour-Impact feedback
• Ask question
Bad question- "the report was wrong. are dumb or did you rush it?"
Good question- "I noticed some errors in the report that impacted my team. what can I do to prevent this?"
• Keep your own ego out of it, be friendly and empathetic
• People are good to understand the sincerity
• Take a pause before replying.
• Ask questions- 
"Is this a good time to keep discussing this?"
"Is there something bigger going on here that you need help with?"
"Is there something about this problem that I am not understanding?"
• Help them solve their problems
• "What would have to be true in order ....?"
• "I am not doubting you, but how can I justify that?"
• Figure out how to stop threatening their ego, Be an ally

7. How to deal with threatened superior
• Talk to him when not giving feedback
• Ask him- "I don't want you to feel threatened, but sometimes I have to give feedback. How can we do that?"
• Being too direct can be threatening to some people 
• "What is your Myers Briggs type?"
• "What is your style?"
• Ask others about it
• Try to let him know in advance- "I know you feel attacked, I am not attacking you"
• Be positive
• Understanding what kind of feedback can work for another person
• Don't put introverts in a room full of strangers and ask to talk
• Don't put extroverts in isolation either

8. confidence vs ego
• Don't say- "I this..", "I that..."
• Say more in interviews, especially if you are female 
• Most important in interview- appearance and enthusiasm
• Don't "I am the best programmer"
Do- "Let me tell you about some of the hard problems I was able to solve"
• Don't- "It was because of me, we won this.."
Do- "I had the privilege of working on a challenging project, can I show you the final results?"

9. When the ego is useful
• To handle false criticism
• "Hey, I appreciate your input. but my self worth is not solely based on your opinion"

title: Insider tips on accelerating career development
description:
This video has been updated. Find it here- https://youtu.be/CeSQwqvIfhU
What is the "secret" to a good career development plan?  Or more simply put, what will give you a clear and effective plan for your career?


I had a revelation this weekend while researching what titles lead people to read further into what is written.  When it comes to personal development, most people would like to hear that there is a quick, secret way to success.  I think this is natural, looking for a shortcut.


With a career, there are few shortcuts.  However, there can be insights, or what I’d call tips, that can make you more effective day after day. So that after a relatively short period of time (a few years), you have pulled far ahead of peers in your career.  After all, why are some people CEOs in their 20s (imagine the list of tech CEOs who have done this) while others are stuck unhappily in mid-level jobs that they no longer like in their 40’s or 50’s?  More than just luck or even skill typically sets them apart.


I would argue that most hyper-successful individuals have a career plan, even if it is subconscious and very simple.  In my next Twitch broadcast, I’ll discuss what I believe forms the basis of a good career plan and the “simple secret” of making your own.

title: Hiring Interns at Amazon | The biggest headhunt in the world
description:
Come understand the fully modern job hunt from the INSIDE.  I’m bringing my longtime friend and coworker, Albert Kim, onto my Twitch broadcast Monday night to discuss how Amazon searches for talent at scale.  Today as I write, the Amazon website has more than 14,000 full-time positions open.  Albert leads “University Programs,” for the Americas, responsible for hiring thousands of interns and full-time new graduates every year.  He and I will talk about the new world of automated resume scans and online assessments amidst a shortage of supply.

This discussion will be essential for students in any discipline to understand where large corporate recruiting is headed.  However, it is also valuable for any manager or job seeker on either side of the talent wars because you’ll get insight into the competitive landscape of today.  We’ll talk about how in 2019 Amazon has reviewed hundreds of thousands of resumes and candidates, a reality that must be the same at Facebook, Google, Microsoft, and other large employers.

Whether you are planning your career, looking for a job, or looking for talent, you want to understand the new job marketplace reality.  You’ll walk away knowing how to navigate the new system-driven reality.

title: How to Be Smarter and More Effective at Work
description:
Make yourself smarter? Can this be done? Probably not. But you can become much more skilled, and in most cases honing your skills to perfection will get you more than raw smarts. We all know the super-smart person who just can’t seem to get much done. In this show, we’ll talk about how to tackle systematic self improvement. Part inspiration and part perspiration, if you want to at least seem smarter, this show is for you.  We’ll also walk through the EZ Coach’s recommended book list. Bring your own book, blog, or podcast recommendations and let’s talk!

title: Joining as CEO in 24 hr Notice | Leading as an Interim CEO | Ft. Ken Myer
description:
Everyone starts new jobs, projects, and internal roles well. Organizations change and suddenly we have to meet new peers, bosses, and employees. The EZ Coach discussed how to do this well on May 28th. He was joined by special guest Ken Myer, a professional interim CEO. Ken routinely joins companies on as little as 24 hours of notice when they have lost their CEO and quickly need someone who can provide continuity and leadership until a new permanent person is located. As a result, Ken has a wealth of wisdom to share on how to effectively start a new project or role.

title: So you want to be a Manager?
description:
What to consider before becoming a manager and how to succeed in being a good one.

Are you considering management? Or have you found yourself thrust into a leadership role, perhaps due to an open role, a departure, or an obvious gap?  The truth is, almost no one is trained as a personnel manager before becoming one.  Instead, we learn on the job, perhaps assisted by a few remedial courses provided long after the fact by the HR department.  How can you know if it is the right thing for you?  And if you are starting down that path now, how can you plan to succeed?  Join me, Ethan Evans, for a lively hour long discussion of your top questions, aided by input by our helpful community of like-minded professionals.

title: How Should I Choose My Next Role, Company, or Job?
description:
You don’t like your job and you want out.  You want to find a new role in your company.  But change can be scary.  Maybe the devil you know is better than where you will wind up?

Learn how to plan for the position you want and go land it.  Discuss the many factors in a new role.  Learn how to discover what will really satisfy you.

“Never run from something; run to something.”  Unpack this advice and understand how to know you are following it.

Ask Ethan Evans about these topics and more.  Hear from him and our community of like-minded professionals to make your plan for your next big step.

title: How Can I Get the Most from Feedback and Performance Reviews?
description:
Have you ever been shocked by unexpected feedback or a poor review and struggled with how to respond? 

Have you had your performance review and walked out wondering exactly what it meant?

Performance reviews influence your salary, your promotion potential, and your access to new roles.  Feedback is your lifeline to discovering and addressing your blind spots, but can be painful and disturbing to hear.

How you prepare for and respond to your performance review, or how you take feedback, can be critical to your success.

Learn the one perfect response to all feedback.

Hear tactics to prepare for your review before you meet with your manager and how to follow up. Discuss these and other key challenges, or ask your own questions and get input from Ethan and other motivated professionals like you!
